thought_title: Called through the cross as his members

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Φεύγετε οὖν τὰς κακὰς παραφυάδας τὰς γεννώσας καρπὸν θανατηφόρον, οὗ ἐὰν γεύσηταί τις, παῤ αὐτὰ ἀποθνήσκει. οὗτοι γὰρ οὔκ εἰσιν φυτεία πατρός, 2, εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν, ἐφαίνοντο ἂν κλάδοι τοῦ σταυροῦ, καὶ ἦν ἂν ὁ καρπὸς αὐτῶν ἄφθαρτος: δἰ οὗ ἐν τῷ πάθει αὐτοῦ προσκαλεῖταν ὑμᾶς ὄντας μέλη αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: Flee, then, the evil offshoots that bear death-bringing fruit; if anyone tastes it, he dies on the spot. For these are not a planting of the Father. For if they were, they would appear as branches of the cross, and their fruit would be incorruptible; through which, in his suffering, he calls you, who are his members.
pass_b_english: So run from those evil offshoots. Their fruit brings death, and whoever tastes it dies at once. These are not the Father's planting (Matthew 15:13).
If they were, they would show themselves as branches of the cross, and their fruit would never decay. Through that cross, in his suffering, he calls you, for you are his members.

choices.why: Botanical: side-shoots growing off the stock; sets up 'planting' and 'branches'.
Echo of Matthew 15:13 (πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου).
Incorruptible fruit in plain words; keeps the contrast with deadly fruit.
Relative most naturally refers back to the cross (σταυροῦ); English names it to avoid an ambiguous 'which'.
Participle gives the ground of the call; 'members' keeps the body image that the next sentence (outside span) develops.

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned; ANF 'the cross by which he calls you' matches the Greek relative.

bible_refs.note: πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται. Lake XML bibl reads 15:16, likely scan error.

notes: Span = Trallians 11.1 and the first part of 11.2, ending at μέλη αὐτοῦ, matching the ANF span. Not translated: the closing sentence of 11.2 (οὐ δύναται οὖν κεφαλὴ χωρὶς γεννηθῆναι ἄνευ μελῶν …).

Source problems in the Lake XML copy: a stray section marker '2,' sits inside the sentence; προσκαλεῖταν is a typo for προσκαλεῖται; παῤ αὐτά = παραυτά ('at once'); δἰ = δι'. source_text keeps the file text as printed.
Lake's XML margin marks 'Mt 15, 16'; the wording (φυτεία … πατρός) matches Matthew 15:13, so 15:13 is tagged. The '16' is likely a scan error.
'Christ' is not supplied in Pass B; the subject of προσκαλεῖται stays 'he' as in the Greek.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked clause by clause. Greek 'Φεύγετε οὖν τὰς κακὰς παραφυάδας τὰς γεννώσας καρπὸν θανατηφόρον, οὗ ἐὰν γεύσηταί τις, παῤ αὐτὰ ἀποθνήσκει' matches Pass A 'Flee, then, the evil offshoots that bear death-bringing fruit; if anyone tastes it, he dies on the spot' and Pass B 'So run from those evil offshoots. Their fruit brings death, and whoever tastes it dies at once'. Negation 'οὔκ εἰσιν φυτεία πατρός' is kept ('are not a planting of the Father' / 'are not the Father's planting'). Counterfactual 'εἰ γὰρ ἦσαν, ἐφαίνοντο ἂν κλάδοι τοῦ σταυροῦ, καὶ ἦν ἂν ὁ καρπὸς αὐτῶν ἄφθαρτος' stays 'if they were ... would' in both. Indicative 'προσκαλεῖταν ὑμᾶς ὄντας μέλη αὐτοῦ' (disclosed typo for προσκαλεῖται) is 'he calls you', not counterfactual; 'δι' οὗ' is 'through which' in A and 'Through that cross' in B, the masculine antecedent being σταυροῦ. '(Matthew 15:13)' sits beside the φυτεία πατρός echo as identified in the supplied notes. Stray '2,' is disclosed and not translated. Title names the call through the cross, not only the locus.
